sentences.text: One line says you’re somewhere along it.
Two lines, taken at the same moment, cross at a point.
You take a bearing on one object, then quickly on another, and draw both lines.
Where they cross is where you are.
Mark it with a small circle, and write the time.
Now, which two objects do you pick?
Choose a pair whose bearings are sixty to ninety degrees apart.
Why not two that are close together?
Because when lines cross at a shallow angle, a one-degree error in either bearing slides the crossing a long way along the line.
Lines that cross near a right angle forgive small errors.
And take the two bearings quickly, one right after the other, so the boat hasn’t moved between them.
